w: On 14 June 1970, in London, the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj were taken in a grand procession along the main streets of the city, and the murti pratishtha in the mandir was performed in a divine way according to the scriptural rites. Through the media, this news had reached everywhere. On this day an author named Peter Brent came to meet Yogiji Maharaj. He had also tried to meet Swamishri in India. He was writing a book on the guru and disciple relationship. In that connection he asked many questions.
Peter: "How do you recognise whether a disciple is able to walk on this path of spiritual practice or not?"
Swamishri: "When God inspires, one recognises that this soul will be able to walk on this path and that one will not. Without the inspiration of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, one cannot recognise it at all."
Peter: "Is the guru God?"
Swamishri: "He is a form of God."

As Peter found this idea hard to understand, Swamishri explained to him the meaning of guru: "The one who removes ignorance and gives light, gives knowledge, is the guru. Towards him the feeling arises that he is a form of God... One who is shrotriya and brahmanishtha is called a guru. Shrotriya means one who gives the true meaning of every word, and brahmanishtha means one who has become brahmarup. A guru who has come through a lineage of gurus is a true guru." (That is, the guru's guru should also be shrotriya and brahmanishtha.)
Peter: "In Christianity there is a doctrine that the whole world is bad. Those born into it do not observe celibacy, so they are bad. So what is your view? Is there nothing good at all?"

Swamishri: "In the view of the Satpurush, nothing at all is bad. A person may be bad at first, but the Satpurush purifies him and leads him on this path, so he cannot be called bad. The world is perishable and worthless, but the pure spiritual seekers in it are drawn to this path. It cannot be said that everything is bad."

Finally he asked a question: if there was anything he had missed asking, would Swamishri tell him. Very naturally, Swamishri said, "If we take a guru who is shrotriya and brahmanishtha, he gives us knowledge of the atma and Paramatma, and we find peace. So search for such a guru and take his refuge."

On 14 June 1970 in London, the procession of the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj went with great splendour along the main roads of the city of London, and the murti pratishtha (installation ceremony) in the mandir took place in a divine way according to the scriptural rites. The news reached everywhere through the media. On this day a writer named Peter Brent came to meet Yogiji Maharaj. He had also tried to meet Swamishri in India. He was writing a book on the guru and disciple relationship. In that connection he asked many questions.
Peter: "How do you recognise whether a disciple is able to walk this path of spiritual endeavour or not?"
Swamishri: "When God inspires, one recognises that this soul will be able to walk this path and that one will not. Without the inspiration of Bhagwan Swaminarayan it cannot be recognised at all."
Peter: "Is the guru God?"
Swamishri: "He is a form of God."

As Peter found this idea hard to understand, Swamishri explained to him the meaning of guru: "One who removes ignorance and gives light, gives knowledge, is the guru. Towards him the feeling arises that he is a form of God... One who is shrotriya and brahmanishtha is called a guru. Shrotriya means one who gives the true meaning of every word, and brahmanishtha means one who has become brahmarup. A guru who has come through the guru parampara (succession of gurus) is the true guru." (That is, the guru's guru must also be shrotriya and brahmanishtha.)
Peter: "In Christianity there is a principle that the whole world is bad. Those born into it do not observe celibacy, so they are bad. So what is your view? Is there nothing good at all?"

Swamishri: "In the view of the Satpurush there is nothing bad at all. A person may be bad at first, but the Satpurush purifies him and leads him on this path, so he cannot be called bad. The world is perishable, it is worthless, but the pure seekers in it are drawn to this path. It cannot be said that everything is bad."

Finally he asked one more question: "If there is anything I have missed asking, please tell me." Very naturally Swamishri said, "If we take a guru who is shrotriya and brahmanishtha, he gives the knowledge of the atma and Paramatma and we attain peace. So one should search for such a guru and take his refuge."

At night Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having his meal (offered first to Thakorji). Narendraprasad Swami said, "In the whole world, everyone takes in oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide. But you are the only person who gives out only oxygen and spreads it across the whole world. Everyone lives by your power."
While eating, Swamishri burst out laughing and, covering his face with both hands, said, "But what if people take in less oxygen?"

Before Swamishri, a satsangi youth delivered a speech about Bhagatji Maharaj in the Italian language. In the evening, the Paris Kishore mandal performed a drama on Khima Dobariya's resolute faith in Lord Swaminarayan.

During weekends a BAPS volunteer sincerely offers his services in the mandir. Subsequently, the department he serves in has progressed tremendously. But because of his duties and responsibilities the volunteer does not attend the Sunday spiritual discourses. His co-volunteers requested Swamishri to instruct him to attend. Swamishri advised the volunteer, “The service you are performing is not wrong. It is really good of you to do it. But everyone should attend the Sunday assembly. Without that your service is of no value. If you do not have spiritual knowledge and understanding then you will fall from Satsang. Therefore you must have the habit of listening to spiritual discourses. You know what Yogiji Maharaj used to say. You must attend the Sunday assembly even if you have to forgo a profit of Rs. 25,000. Then why are you incurring such a loss upon yourself! Take a pledge to attend the Sunday assembly. If you do not attend the Sunday assembly then you’ll not progress. Shriji Maharaj has said that if one does not listen to spiritual discourses then one will not attain virtues in life. So, take a pledge today. Our organisation stands on the strength of spiritual discourses.”
Swamishri inspired a volunteer to strengthen his Satsang foundations by attending the Sunday spiritual assembly.

Swamishri said, "We are talking with God."

The evening satsang assembly celebrated Kishore-Kishori and Yuvak-Yuvati Day. More than 2,500 youths had assembled in the Yogi Sabhagruh. In all, there were 9,900 devotees and youths. When Swamishri arrived, a drama ‘Ek Daglu’ was in progress. Thereafter Swamishri was honoured with garlands. In his blessings Swamishri praised, “Kishore mandal ni jai . The reason behind the Kishore Mandal’s enthusiasm and faithful effort is the motive to please Maharaj, Swami, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Outside, many programmes are held to please and entertain others, but one will not gain values and inner purity. However, when one becomes associated with and committed to satsang, one realizes its importance, and then one nourishes the feeling of what one can do for God and his Sadhu. By indulging in material joys, one invites misery and pain. No matter how wealthy one is infatuation for worldly pleasures does not give peace. And conversely, when one has no wealth but savours satsang, one is blessed with peace.”
Failure and faith

3 June 2009, Mumbai A youth had titled his letter to Swamishri, ‘God does not exist 100%’. The reasons he gave were as follows, “I failed six times in the eligibility exam to go abroad. Then the agent ran away with Rs.50,000 that I had paid. I tried to obtain visas for USA and England but failed. You had blessed me, but there was no success. I had offered abhishek to Nilkanth Varni but to no avail. In every endeavour I have failed miserably. So, God does not exist! Others get success and why am I a victim of failure?” Swamishri advised the youth by phone, “God exists. He is the all-doer. It is his wish that prevails. Your failure is no reason to believe that he does not exist. Believe him to be the all-doer, do your puja daily and attend satsang. Pray daily so that you can get good thoughts. Do not lose hope and courage in spite of your failures. Maharaj had blessed Dada Khachar a number of times and yet his work remained undone. But he never left Maharaj! So be strong, feel hopeful and engage yourself in bhajan. God will do good for you.”
Solution to depression

4 June 2009, Mumbai A youth was suffering from depression. Swamishri reassured him, “Always chant God’s name. You have a house, parents, relatives, … Then why are you depressed? God is also with you. Why do you worry? Remember Maharaj. I will also pray for you.”Swamishri reminded him of all that he had and thus infused hope and strength.
Praising a devotee

9 June 2009, Mumbai Dr Bhagubhai Patel is 98-years-old. He had served Shastriji Maharaj and offered his services as a doctor to Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Presently, because of old age, he suffers from amnesia and poor eyesight. He spends his time saying mala , doing bhajan and arti all day. On seeing him Swamishri started singing his praises, “You do a lot of bhajan. You have served both Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. They have blessed you. You have the association of Maharaj so may you be blessed with Akshardham while doing bhajan. Your sons are good. They serve you with care and respect. The reason for this is that you have offered devotion to God. I am very happy that you have come, and I have had your darshan. The sadhus have also got your darshan. Everyone is pleased to see you.” Swamishri expressed his respect for and sang the praises of a dedicated and genuine devotee.
Comforting a devotee

15 June 2009, Mumbai A devotee and his wife had gone on vacation to Darjeeling, West Bengal. During a boat ride his wife mistakenly fell into the lake and was drowned. The devotee was in deep shock. He remained cloistered in his home and had not attended to his business since the tragedy occurred fifteen days ago. Swamishri blessed the devotee and advised him, “It was her fate to die in that manner. Now instead of remaining depressed and paralysed pray for her soul. You will experience peace within. Chant Swaminarayan, Swaminarayan. Say five malas daily. Do bhajan. It will give peace to her soul too.”

Shri K.K., CEO of the Coca Cola company in India, came for darshan. In Gandhinagar Pramukh Swami Maharaj had given him a mala. He turns that mala every day, and all the office bearers of the Coca Cola company worldwide who come to India, he first brings to Akshardham.
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "By having darshan of God, the intellect becomes good."
K.K. said, "At your darshan there is great, great peace."
Swamishri said, "If you work keeping faith in God, God takes care, and by keeping faith in God there is no burden on us. Thinking, 'I did it, I did it,' creates a burden."

K.K. said, "But I keep my attention only on you, and that alone gives me peace." Having said this, he added, "Actually I had no desire to become CEO. I had intended to retire and engage in seva in your organisation."

There was a letter from a youth. This youth, who had gone to serve at a mandir in America, had savings of 63,000 rupees. His wish was to give it for the seva of the New Jersey Akshardham. After reading the letter, Pramukh Swami Maharaj dictated a reply: "The seva you have done there with your body is a great seva, and all seva is included in it. Your feeling itself is a great seva. For now, do not think of doing financial seva."

K.K. said, "Your darshan brings very, very great peace."

ds.t: Your seva with the body is great
w: There was a letter from a youth. This youth, who had gone to a mandir in America for seva, had savings of 63,000 rupees. His wish was to offer them as seva for the New Jersey Akshardham. After reading the letter, Pramukh Swami Maharaj had a reply written, "The seva you have done there with your body is a great seva; all seva is included in it. Your feeling itself is a great seva. For now, do not think of making a financial offering."

Today Yogichintandas Swami asked Mahant Swami Maharaj, "Swami! Even when we are being hypocritical, we often do not realise that we are being hypocritical; it seems genuine. The katha, talks and arti we do all seem good. So how can we know that we are being hypocritical?"
Swamishri said, "Strict introspection."
Yogichintandas Swami asked, "Does introspection mean looking at you?"

Swamishri said, "No. One should think, 'Is everything I do genuine? Is there any trace at all of deceit in it?' Shake yourself up. Instead, we shake up others." Swamishri said this, laughing at this petty nature common to all human beings.
Yogichintandas Swami asked, "Once we realise we are being hypocritical, what should we do?"
With feeling, Swamishri said emphatically, "Throw it out. It will hurt, but you will have to throw it out. It will hurt a lot, but if there is a longing for moksha within, kick it out. Get out!"
He said, "One has to be very strict for this."

Swamishri said, "Yes, this satsang is all about introspection. 99% introspection. Instead, we keep looking at others. Introspection turned the wrong way. We have to look within ourselves. If one looks at others, one fills up with rubbish, and if one looks at oneself, one clears the rubbish out."
